decisions.name: TeamIDIsNewtypeOverText
decisions.what: TeamID is a newtype over T.Text
why: Prevents accidental substitution with leagueID, commissioner, or other Text fields.
Custom ToJSON/FromJSON unwrap to bare Text rather than a tagged object.

decisions.name: MultiplierFieldsParsedFromJSONStrings
decisions.what: BattingMults and PitchingMults fields are parsed via parseDouble, which calls withText and reads the contents
why: Source JSON quotes multipliers as strings ("1.0") rather than numeric literals.
withText on a numeric value will fail; the schema requires string-typed multipliers.

decisions.name: DraftAndLineupLimitsAreSeparateRecords
decisions.what: DraftRosterLmts and LgLineupLmts have parallel positional fields but distinct types
why: Draft caps and lineup caps are independently configured in the JSON schema.
Field-name prefixes (dr_ vs lg_) prevent record-field collisions.
sumDraftRosterLmts only sums the dr_ side; LgLineupLmts has its own consumers in queryLgLineupLmts.

unwrapTeamID: extracts the inner Text from a TeamID newtype
sumDraftRosterLmts: sums all 9 positional fields of DraftRosterLmts (catcher through r_pitcher)
parseDouble: uses withText, then reads :: [(Double, String)] requiring full parse with empty remainder
fails the parser with 'Could not parse double from string' on numeric JSON or malformed text
consumed by every field in BattingMults FromJSON and PitchingMults FromJSON

decisions.name: PlayerIDstringIsUnused
decisions.what: PlayerIDstring newtype is defined but has no consumers in the codebase
why: Defined alongside PlayerID but never constructed or pattern-matched outside its own definition.
Dead code; safe to delete.

decisions.name: OfficialRosterFromJSONWalksHashMap
decisions.what: FromJSON OfficialRoster manually walks the officialPlayers HashMap via HM.elems
why: Source JSON nests players under an object keyed by player id, not under a JSON array.
dataPulled and checksum are required (.: not .:?), unlike Input.ActiveRoster which makes them optional.
OfficialPlayer instance uses RecordWildCards in its return so all 9 fields are bound by name during parse.

playerIDToText: T.pack . show; produces decimal Int representation
the only path used to convert a PlayerID to a Map key throughout the codebase
textToPlayerID: uses reads :: [(Int, String)] requiring full parse with empty remainder
returns Nothing on any non-Int text
round-trip with playerIDToText holds for any valid Int
unwrapPlayerId: extracts the inner Int from a PlayerID newtype

decisions.name: LgManagerJSONHasComissionerTypo
decisions.what: FromJSON LgManager parses the JSON key 'comissioner' (single 'm') for the commissioner field
why: On-disk JSON files use the misspelled key.
ToJSON LgManager emits 'commissioner' (correct spelling), so write-then-read round-trips will FAIL.
Asymmetric: this can only be fixed by editing both the FromJSON instance and every existing JSON file in lockstep, or by accepting both keys in FromJSON.

decisions.name: LineupAndRosterAreParallelRecords
decisions.what: CurrentLineup and Roster have identical 9-field shape, distinct types, distinct field name suffixes (C vs R)
why: Lineup is the active set per game; Roster is the full owned set.
Field-name suffix prevents Haskell record-field namespace collisions.
Every position-mutating function exists in two parallel forms across Draft and Validators.

decisions.name: JSONFieldNamesUseShortPositionCodes
decisions.what: FromJSON and ToJSON for both CurrentLineup and Roster use 'C', '1B', '2B', '3B', 'SS', 'OF', 'U', 'SP', 'RP' as JSON keys
why: Matches the short-letter convention used in positionCodeToText and positionCodeToOfficialText.
Does NOT match the draft slot names (pitcher, catcher, first, second...) used by Draft and Validators position dispatch.

decisions.name: StatTypeIsTwoConstructorSum
decisions.what: StatType = Batting | Pitching
why: Two-constructor sum forbids the third 'undefined' state a Bool would admit.
Consumed by Validators.batterOrPitcher (lineup-based dispatch), PointCalc.calculatePointsForPlayer (stat-table dispatch), Scraper.statTypeToString and Scraper.seasonStatsUrl (URL construction).
Single point of growth if a third stat category is added.

decisions.name: GmPointsCarriesPlayerIDInline
decisions.what: GmPoints has gmpts_Id; BattingGmPoints has gmb_gameId; PitchingGmPoints has gmp_gameId
why: Earlier design used external (PlayerID, GmPoints) tuples; bundling the ID inline removes the un-zip-then-rezip risk.
Forces PointCalc.mergeGmPoints to defensively check that two GmPoints share a player ID at runtime, returning Left on mismatch.
BUG: gmb_gameId and gmp_gameId are populated with the literal placeholder string 'GameID' in calcBattingPoints and calcPitchingPoints; no real game ID is ever threaded in.

decisions.name: PlayerResultsAndResultsAreDeadCode
decisions.what: PlayerResults and Results data types have no constructors used outside their own definitions
why: PlayerResults was an earlier dispatch shape replaced by direct StatType handling.
Results was an earlier shape for per-team final scoring output that was never wired up.
Both are safe to delete.

decisions.name: DraftOrderStrategyIsAFunctionType
decisions.what: DraftOrderStrategy = Int -> [TeamID] -> [TeamID]; selectDraftOrderStrategy dispatches a Text name to a strategy
why: First-class function value lets callers pick a strategy by config string at runtime.
Unknown strategy names silently fall through to serpentine (the default branch in selectDraftOrderStrategy).

decisions.name: RankingDataTimeFormatIsTimezoneNaive
decisions.what: FromJSON and ToJSON for RankingData use parseTimeM/formatTime with format "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M"
why: No seconds, no timezone offset.
Despite the field type being UTCTime, parses and emissions are timezone-naive in practice.

decisions.name: PlayerRankingsTypeAlias
decisions.what: type PlayerRankings = [PlayerRanking]
why: Aliases [PlayerRanking] for use in mkEmptyRankings's signature.
No other consumers in the codebase.

notes: rounds = totalPicks `div` length teams (integer division; remainder dropped)
alternates teams, reverse teams, teams, reverse teams ... for 'rounds' iterations
rounds = totalPicks `div` length teams
4-round repeating pattern: forward, mid-shifted, reverse, mid-shifted-reverse
mid-shift uses 'drop (length teams `div` 2) $ cycle teams' taking 'length teams' elements
case-sensitive match on 'serpentine' or 'experimental_snake'
any other input falls through to serpentineOrderStrategy

decisions.name: PlayerGameIdBackfilledAfterParse
decisions.what: FromJSON Player sets gameid = Nothing; Scraper.assignGameIdToPlayers populates it later
why: GameId is at the top of the boxscore JSON, not inside individual player records.
Threading parent context through FromJSON would require a custom parser; backfill is structurally simpler.
If a code path forgets the backfill, downstream code sees Nothing and (in playerToJsonPlayerData) emits empty-string Map keys.

decisions.name: GameIdGameDateBackfilledAfterParse
decisions.what: FromJSON GameID sets game_date = Nothing; Scraper.assignDateToSchedule populates it later
why: Same reason as Player.gameid backfill: the date is at a higher level in the schedule JSON than the GameID record.
Backfill runs once per fetched schedule via assignDateToSchedule.

decisions.name: TeamDataFiltersInvalidPlayers
decisions.what: FromJSON TeamData drops players whose allPositions is empty or absent
why: hasValidPositions checks allPositions per-player and returns False for empty/missing lists.
Filtered players never appear in the resulting M.Map.

decisions.name: ActiveRosterMetadataOptional
decisions.what: ActiveRoster's dataPulled and checksum are Maybe Text
why: Source MLB API does not include these fields; Scraper.writeRosterToFile adds them on write.
Asymmetric with OfficialRoster which requires both.

decisions.name: EveryStatFieldIsMaybe
decisions.what: BattingStats has 25 Maybe Int fields; PitchingStats has 45 fields, all Maybe Int except pit_inningsPitched :: Maybe Text
why: MLB Stats API omits fields when the corresponding event didn't occur in the game.
Maybe Int over default-zero pushes the 'absent' vs 'zero' distinction to the consumer; in practice every consumer uses fromMaybe 0.
FromJSON uses .:? on every field so any subset can be absent.

decisions.name: InningsPitchedIsTextNotDouble
decisions.what: pit_inningsPitched :: Maybe Text
why: MLB sends innings as '6.2' meaning 6 and 2/3 innings - the decimal is a sub-third count, not a tenth.
Storing as Text preserves the notation for display; PointCalc.calcPitchingPoints parses to Double via readMaybe, which silently treats '6.2' as 6.2 (not 6.6666...).
BUG: this is wrong by up to 0.06 IP per pitcher per game and affects quality_start gating.

decisions.name: ActivePlayerNestedFieldExtraction
decisions.what: FromJSON ActivePlayer pulls currentTeam, primaryPosition, batSide, pitchHand from nested objects via traverse (.: 'id') or traverse (.: 'code')
why: MLB API returns these as objects with embedded code/id fields; the Haskell type flattens them to Maybe Text/Maybe Int.
If the nested object exists but lacks the inner field, the parse fails (does not silently become Nothing).

decisions.name: PlayerNormalizesEmptyAllPositions
decisions.what: FromJSON Player treats allPositions = Just [] identically to allPositions = Nothing
why: Normalization happens at parse time so consumers don't need to differentiate 'absent' from 'empty list'.
hasValidPositions then returns False for both cases.

hasValidPositions: fromJSON-decodes the Value as Player and checks allPositions is Just non-empty
called by FromJSON TeamData to filter players before they enter the players map
duplicated identically in Validators.hasValidPositions and Input_trace.hasValidPositions

decisions.name: ModuleIsLegacyDuplicateOfInput
decisions.what: Input_trace defines GameData, Teams, TeamData, Player, Person, Position, Status, PlayerStats, BattingStats, PitchingStats, hasValidPositions
why: Earlier version of Input.hs; Player here lacks the gameid field that Input.Player has.
BattingStats and PitchingStats are structurally identical to Input's versions including 25 and 45 Maybe-wrapped fields respectively.
Consumed only by Test.hs main.

hasValidPositions: duplicate of Input.hasValidPositions; uses Input_trace.Player rather than Input.Player
called by FromJSON TeamData in this module to filter players

decisions.name: ModuleIsAlternateInputForSeasonStats
decisions.what: Leaderboard defines its own SeasonData, Teams, TeamData, Player, Person, Status, PlayerSeasonStats, BattingTotals, PitchingTotals
why: BattingTotals (32 fields) is a superset of Input.BattingStats with rate fields (avg, obp, slg, ops, babip, atBatsPerHomeRun) as Maybe Text.
PitchingTotals (59 fields) is a superset of Input.PitchingStats with rate fields (era, whip, strikePercentage, winPercentage, etc.) as Maybe Text.
Player here lacks parentTeamId and allPositions; carries seasonStats instead of stats.
TeamData here does NOT filter empty-allPositions players (unlike Input.TeamData) - traverses parseJSON over the full map.
No consumers in the codebase outside Playground.hs imports, and Playground's body is a large commented-out block.

decisions.name: ToJSONOnlyHere_FromJSONInStats
decisions.what: Middle defines ToJSON for JsonPlayerData, JsonStatsData, I.Position, I.PitchingStats, I.BattingStats, I.ActiveRoster, I.ActivePlayer; Stats.hs defines the FromJSON direction for JsonPlayerData and JsonStatsData
why: Write path (Scraper) and read path (PointCalc) are split across modules.
Field name prefixes (bat_, pit_) match the FromJSON in Stats.
Edits to one direction can drift from the other silently.

decisions.name: ToJSONOmitsNothingFields
decisions.what: ToJSON BattingStats and PitchingStats use catMaybes to skip fields whose Maybe value is Nothing
why: Reduces serialized size given that most stats are absent for any given player-game.
FromJSON in Stats uses .:? on every field, so absence reads back as Nothing.

decisions.name: PositionToJSONReadsTextAsInt
decisions.what: ToJSON I.Position calls 'read (T.unpack pos_code)' to produce a Number
why: The on-disk JSON schema for Middle uses numeric position codes; Input parses them as Text and Middle converts back.
read is partial; non-numeric pos_code values throw at runtime.

decisions.name: ToJSONJsonPlayerDataKeyIsPlayerUnderscoreId
decisions.what: ToJSON JsonPlayerData emits the key 'player_id' (with underscore), not 'playerId'
why: Stats.FromJSON M.JsonPlayerData reads 'player_id' to match.
Inconsistent with the playerId field name used everywhere else in the codebase (camelCase).

decisions.name: ActivePlayerToJSONFlattensNestedFields
decisions.what: ToJSON I.ActivePlayer emits currentTeam, primaryPosition, batSide, pitchHand as scalar values, not nested objects
why: FromJSON ActivePlayer in Input parses these from nested objects (currentTeam.id, primaryPosition.code, etc).
ToJSON output is therefore NOT round-trippable through FromJSON ActivePlayer; the two instances target different schemas.

decisions.name: ActiveRosterToJSONKeysByStringifiedPlayerId
decisions.what: ToJSON I.ActiveRoster builds an officialPlayers object keyed by Text-of-Int playerId
why: Matches the read-side schema in OfficialRoster.FromJSON which walks officialPlayers as a HashMap.
FromJSON ActiveRoster in Input uses a 'people' array, so this ToJSON path bridges to the OfficialRoster schema, not the ActiveRoster schema.

decisions.name: ConversionDefinesItsOwnPlayerType
decisions.what: Conversion.Player is a flat record with String fields, distinct from Input.Player and OfficialRoster.OfficialPlayer
why: Tied to Cassava (Data.Csv) ToNamedRecord and DefaultOrdered for CSV emission.
FromJSON parses a flat object shape (no nested currentTeam.id, no nested primaryPosition.code).
PlayersFile is a newtype around HM.HashMap String Player and parses a top-level 'officialPlayers' object.
Consumed only by FetchActiveRoster.main.

boolToString: consumed by ToNamedRecord Player to encode the active field

decisions.name: ModuleIsAlternateFromJSONForJsonPlayerData
decisions.what: Stats defines GameID, GameIDstring newtypes plus FromJSON instances for Middle.JsonPlayerData, Middle.JsonStatsData, and its own BattingStats/PitchingStats
why: Middle.hs defines ToJSON for JsonPlayerData/JsonStatsData; Stats.hs defines the FromJSON direction.

Stats.BattingStats and Stats.PitchingStats use field names prefixed 'bat_' and 'pit_' (matching Middle's ToJSON output) but are otherwise structurally identical to Input.BattingStats/Input.PitchingStats - a third copy of those types in the codebase.
GameID and GameIDstring newtypes have no consumers in the codebase.

decisions.name: DraftStateIsAFlatRecord
decisions.what: DraftState bundles teams, availablePlayerIds, draftHistory, currentTeamIndex, draftOrder, draftComplete, teamRankings
why: Single record threaded through the recursive draftPlayers loop.
draftComplete is a Bool flag set explicitly by selectNextPlayer's Nothing branch.
currentTeamIndex is an index into draftOrder, not into teams.
Has Show and Eq instances; Eq is used by draftCycle to detect 'no progress made' via newState == state.

decisions.name: DraftLoopIsRecursiveIO
decisions.what: draftPlayers is a recursive IO action; no State monad
why: Only IO effect is putStrLn on error.
Errors abort the loop and return the pre-failure state.

decisions.name: DraftConfigBundlesConfigAndPlayers
decisions.what: DraftConfig has two fields: cfg :: C.Configuration and officialPlayers :: [O.OfficialPlayer]
why: Avoids re-passing both arguments through every helper that needs them.
Constructed once per draft run by AutoDraft.main.

instantiateDraft: filters teamRankings by 'PR.teamId r `elem` C.teamId config'
calls Utility.generateDraftOrder which uses System.Random.Shuffle.shuffleM (IO randomness, no seed)
creates one R.LgManager per teamId with empty lineup and roster

notes: loops until draftComplete is True OR draftCycle returns a Just error
on error, prints 'Error: <msg>' and returns the PRE-error state
no pick limit beyond what selectNextPlayer enforces by exhaustion

updateState: looks up the team by teamId in DraftState.teams via find
calls addToRosterAndLineup; if isNewPlayer is False, returns the unchanged state
uses fromJust on the find result; aborts at runtime if teamId is not in teams
draftCycle: looks up the team by teamId in [(tid, t) | t@(R.LgManager _ _ tid _ _ _) <- teams state]
filters officialPlayers by availablePlayerIds, calls selectNextPlayer
Nothing from selectNextPlayer sets draftComplete = True with no error
checks newState == state via the Eq instance to detect 'no progress made' and reports 'Failed to add player to roster or lineup'
runDraftCycle: thin wrapper around draftCycle taking a teamState argument
selectNextPlayer: finds the team's RankingData, extracts ranked playerIds in order
returns the first available OfficialPlayer whose id appears in the rankedPlayerIds list
Nothing if no ranked player is still available - this terminates the WHOLE draft, not just this team
addToRosterAndLineup: pitcher path: addPitcherToRoster picks s_pitcher or r_pitcher slot; addPlayerToLineup uses the chosen slot
non-pitcher path: addBatterToRoster checks the position cap; addPlayerToLineup adds if cap allows
returns ((Roster, CurrentLineup), Bool) where Bool indicates whether anything was added to the roster
addPlayerToLineup: case-by-case dispatch on position Text against 9 lineup slots
if slot is at or above its lg_* cap, returns lineup unchanged with no signal to caller
addPlayerToPosition: case-by-case dispatch on position Text against 9 roster slots
addPitcherToRoster: fills s_pitcher up to dr_s_pitcher cap, then r_pitcher up to dr_r_pitcher cap
returns (roster, "") when both pitcher caps are reached
empty-string return is the 'no slot available' signal consumed by addToRosterAndLineup
addBatterToRoster: consults queryDraftRosterLmts for the cap; appends via addPlayerToPosition if under cap
returns (roster, False) when at or above cap

mergeGmPoints: compares gmpts_Id of both arguments; returns Left 'Attempting to merge points for different players!' on mismatch
on match: concatenates gmpts_batting and gmpts_pitching lists
does not re-sum total_points across the merged lists

notes: calls Validators.batterOrPitcher to determine StatType from the LgManager's lineup
looks up M.JsonStatsData via MS.lookup (O.playerIDToText playerId) in stats
Batting branch returns Left 'Batting stats not found' if the lookup or M.batting is Nothing
Pitching branch returns Left 'Pitching stats not found' if the lookup or M.pitching is Nothing

calcBattingPoints: single = bat_hits - (bat_doubles + bat_triples + bat_homeRuns), each via fromMaybe 0
gmb_gameId is hardcoded to the literal string "GameID"
gmb_total_points is computed at construction as the sum of all weighted contributions
calcPitchingPoints: this reads MLB '6.2' (= 6 and 2/3 innings) as the literal Double 6.2
quality_start awarded when actualInnings >= 6 AND pit_earnedRuns <= 3
negative contributions: pit_baseOnBalls, pit_hits, pit_earnedRuns, pit_hitBatsmen, pit_losses
gmp_gameId is hardcoded to the literal string "GameID"
gmp_total_points is computed at construction as the sum of all weighted contributions

decisions.name: BoxscoreFetchSkipsLiveGames
decisions.what: fetchFinishedBxScore checks codedGameState == 'F' before fetching the boxscore
why: Only finished games have stable boxscore stats.
Returns Right Nothing for non-final games; downstream filterFinishedGames removes them.

decisions.name: ConcurrentFetchUnboundedAsync
decisions.what: fetchFinishedBxScores uses Control.Concurrent.Async.mapConcurrently
why: Parallelizes per-game HTTP fetches across an entire day's gameId list.
No bound on concurrency; no retry or rate-limit handling.

fetchGameScheduleForDate: fetches via scheduleUrl date, decodes as GameSchedule
calls assignDateToSchedule to backfill game_date on every GameID
fetchGameStatus: fetches via gameStatusUrl gameId, decodes as LiveGameWrapper
fetchFinishedBxScore: two-step: status fetch then conditional boxscore fetch
Right (Just GameData) for finished games; Right Nothing for in-progress; Left for fetch/parse errors
calls assignGameIdToPlayers on the boxscore before returning
fetchFinishedBxScores: mapConcurrently over [Int]; sequenceA collapses [Either] to Either []
filters out (gameId, Nothing) entries via 'finishedGames' so the resulting Map only contains finished games
fetchFinishedBxScoresToJsonPlayerData: calls fetchFinishedBxScores and applies convertGameDataMapToJsonPlayerData on success

notes: iterates generateDateRange start end with mapM_ processDate
no transactionality; failures on later dates do not unwind earlier successes

processDate: fetches schedule, calls processAndPrintGames (which only prints), then re-fetches and writes stats via writeDataToFile
filename comes from formatFilename date, written under 'appData/stats'
flattenedPlayersList: id function on Map Text JsonPlayerData
processAndPrintGames: if hasGamesForDate is True, fetches boxscores and discards them; otherwise prints 'No games scheduled for the provided date.'
fetchActiveRoster: fetches via rosterUrl season, decodes as I.ActiveRoster
writeRosterToFile: encodes only people via encode (I.people roster) to compute the checksum
checksum covers ONLY the people field, not the full ActiveRoster
writes the full ActiveRoster (with checksum and dataPulled set) as JSON to path
assignDateToSchedule: sets game_date on every GameID inside every DateEntry to the provided Text date
assignGameIdToPlayers: sets gameid on every Player in both away and home teams to Just gameId
hasGamesForDate: True iff any DateEntry has Just games (regardless of whether the inner Vector is empty)
extractGameIds: concatenates I.gamePk values across all DateEntry.games vectors
writeDataToFile: createDirectoryIfMissing on the path, writes encode dataToSave to path ++ '/' ++ filename
playerToJsonPlayerData: stats = single-entry Map keyed by 'maybe "" (T.pack . show) gameid'
if Player.gameid is Nothing (assignGameIdToPlayers not called), the map key is the empty string
playerToJsonStatsData: allPositions defaults to [] when Player.allPositions is Nothing
convertGameDataMapToJsonPlayerData: concatMap gameDataToPlayerDataPairs over Map elements (mapMaybe id drops Nothings first)
rawStringToText replaces escaped backslash and quote sequences in the key
mergeJsonStatsData: discards the first argument; returns the second unchanged
second argument always wins on key collision
formatFilename: replaces '-' with '_' and appends '.json' to the date string
stringToDay: parseTimeOrError True defaultTimeLocale '%Y-%m-%d'; partial on bad input

decisions.name: PositionStringConvertersAreSeparate
decisions.what: Four functions convert between position naming conventions: positionTextToOfficialCode, positionCodeToText, positionCodeToOfficialText, positionCodeToDraftText
why: Three input conventions exist: numeric scorekeeper codes ('1'-'10'), short letters ('P','C','1B','2B' etc), draft slot names ('pitcher','catcher','first','outfield').
All four use catch-all '_ -> "Unknown"' which silently swallows typos and new positions.
positionCodeToDraftText composes positionCodeToOfficialText with an inner officialTextToDraftText helper.

positionCodeToDraftText: composes positionCodeToOfficialText with an inner conversion to draft slot names
mkLgManagers: one R.LgManager per teamId in config; each with mkEmptyLineup and mkEmptyRoster
mkLgManagersWithFilter: same as mkLgManagers but iterates over a provided [TeamID] subset
createLgManager: constructs an R.LgManager from config plus explicit teamId, lineup, roster
extendRankingsWithUnrankedPlayers: appends every PlayerID not already in rankedPlayers (preserving allPlayerIds order) after the ranked ones
generateRandomSHA256: 32 random bytes hashed with SHA256, hex-encoded as Text
createRandomTeamID: C.TeamID wrapping the full hex SHA256 output (callers truncate via T.take 12 for short forms)
shuffleList: no consumers in the codebase outside Generators.main
removeAt: uses splitAt n; partial on the cons pattern when n is out of range
withEither: runs the IO action; on Left prints to stdout (not stderr); on Right calls the handler
eitherToMaybe: Right b -> Just b; otherwise Nothing
fetchAndDecodeJSON: parseRequest_ is partial on malformed URLs
loadDataFromDir: lists JSON files via listJsonFiles, reads each with readJson
filterInvalidRankings: keeps RankingData whose teamId is in the provided [TeamID] list
filterValidTeams: keeps TeamIDs that appear in the rankings list
findPlayerRanking: find the PlayerRanking by playerId, return its rank
computeChecksum: BL.toStrict then SHA256 hash, hex-encoded as Text
randomizeOrder: = shuffleM via System.Random.Shuffle; uses MonadIO randomness with no seed
generateDraftOrder: filterValidTeams to drop teams without rankings, then randomizeOrder, then apply selectDraftOrderStrategy from config.draft_parameters.order

decisions.name: InvertedReturnConventionForUniqueChecks
decisions.what: hasUniqueLineupPlayers and hasUniqueRosterPlayers return Left when there are no duplicates and Right when there are
why: Left value carries the success message string; Right value carries the duplicate PlayerID list.
Inverts the conventional Either bias used elsewhere in the module.

extractNameFromPath: reverse . takeWhile (/= '/') . reverse - returns the basename
processConfigResults: iterates [(FileName, FileContent)], printing extractNameFromPath fname before each testLineup call
testLineup: prints the parsed LgManager and lineup, then runs validateAndPrintLineup
Left input prints 'Failed to parse Roster JSON: <err>'
findPlayer: find by playerId AND playerId being in the availableIds list
consumed by Draft (transitively via Validators import)
maxPossibleTeams: minimum of maxPossibleTeamsForPosition over the hardcoded list ['P','C','1B','2B','3B','SS','LF','CF','RF','DH']
maxPossibleTeamsForPosition: draftLimit derivation: pitcher = dr_s_pitcher + dr_r_pitcher; outfield = dr_outfield * 3 (assumes LF/CF/RF interchangeable); others use the single matching dr_* field

result is playerCount `div` draftLimit when draftLimit > 0, else 0
isLineupValid: validateLineup manager config; True iff Right
getRosterValidationErrors: validateLineup despite the name; returns the Left list or []
getLineupValidationErrors: validateLineup; returns the Left list or []
hasUniqueLineupPlayers: Left 'No duplicate players found.' when allPlayers \\ nub allPlayers is empty
hasUniqueRosterPlayers: Left 'No duplicate players found in roster.' on success
lookupPlayerInRoster: True if playerId appears in any of the 9 roster slots
lookupPlayerInLineup: True if playerId appears in any of the 9 lineup slots
getRosterDiscrepancies: for each of 9 positions: Just (posName, length players - limit) when length > limit, else Nothing
getLineupDiscrepancies: for each of 9 positions: Just (posName, length players - limit) when length > limit, else Nothing
countPlayersOnRoster: case-by-case dispatch on position Text against 9 roster slot names
countPlayersInLineup: case-by-case dispatch on position Text against 9 lineup slot names

notes: calls getRosterDiscrepancies and hasUniqueRosterPlayers
returns Right () when discrepancies is empty AND duplicateCheck is Left (the inverted convention)
Left contains either the duplicate-IDs-as-strings list with a trailing 'Duplicate player IDs found in roster.' message, or per-position overage messages
calls getLineupDiscrepancies and hasUniqueLineupPlayers
Right () when discrepancies is empty AND duplicateCheck is Left
same Left structure as validateRoster but with 'Duplicate player IDs found in lineup.'
IO action returning Bool
prints discrepancies to stdout; calls validatePlayerId (which prints) and hasUniqueLineupPlayers (printed via the inverted convention)
True only when validPositions AND validRosterSize AND all player IDs valid AND no duplicates

queryLimits: dispatches 'draft' -> queryDraftRosterLmts, 'lineup' -> queryLgLineupLmts; anything else returns 0
queryDraftRosterLmts: case-by-case dispatch on position Text against 9 dr_* fields; catch-all returns 0
queryLgLineupLmts: case-by-case dispatch on position Text against 9 lg_* fields; catch-all returns 0
hasValidPositions: no internal consumers in this module
lookupPlayerId: reads testFiles/appData/rosters/activePlayers.json on every call via readJson
returns False on parse failure or on textToPlayerID returning Nothing
validatePlayerId: Right 'All Players are valid.' when all players exist in the on-disk active roster
getUniquePlayerIdsLineup: name claims uniqueness but the function does NOT deduplicate (it just flattens)
validatePositionCount: Just (posName, overage) when length players > maxAllowed, else Nothing
totalPlayersInLineup: sum of lengths of all 9 CurrentLineup fields
validateCurrentLineup: Bool: True when getLineupDiscrepancies is empty AND hasUniqueLineupPlayers returns Left (the inverted-success case)
findPlayerPosition: checks 9 lineup slots labeled C, 1B, 2B, 3B, SS, U, OF, SP, RP
Right pos if exactly one slot contains the playerId
Left 'Player not found in current lineup.' if zero matches
Left 'Player found in multiple positions in the lineup.' if 2+ matches

notes: batterPositions = [cC, b1C, b2C, b3C, ssC, uC, ofC]
pitcherPositions = [spC, rpC]
Right Batting if playerName is in any batter list; Right Pitching if in any pitcher list; Left otherwise

analyzeDraftResults: prints 'Team 1 Draft Analysis:' and 'Team 2 Draft Analysis:' headers; calls analyzeTeamDraft for each
linesToPrint caps the per-team output via printAnalysis
analyzeTeamDraft: builds rankingMap from rank to PlayerID; produces [(rank, playerId, drafted)] sorted by rank
getAllPlayerIdsFromTeam: concatenates all 9 roster fields and all 9 lineup fields
printAnalysis: take linesToPrint over the sorted analysis list
